_doc: Negative-proof ledger. A control is trusted only after an attributed failure on deliberate broken input and a verified restored pass.

gates.description: agent-settings#1124: the pinned provider-free resolver and the single Hermes gmail_reply entrypoint must stay within the reviewed fail-closed metadata, preview, body, and two-provider send flow.

observedFailure.breakApplied: The guard was deliberately given a hostile consumer whose only resolver call is unreachable and whose send body takes unchecked raw bytes from args.
observedFailure.restoredPass: The same command with skills/productivity/google-workspace/scripts/google_api.py restored as --consumer returned status=pass, findings=[], copySha256=7f80fb768cd3082bf1546e6694c0cdc924ad346742389988659dc3c510160de3, exit 0. The canonical test runner then passed 34 focused tests across two files, including both provider branches and ten poison-send denial cases.
observedFailure.proofScope: Pinned-copy integrity and deliberately narrow static adoption in gmail_reply: exact metadata binding, directly reachable fail-closed resolver assignment, canonical MIME body derivation, and exactly one approved send call per provider branch. The focused synthetic example.test suite separately covers Reply-To precedence, case-sensitive mailbox local parts, domain normalization, RFC 2047 subjects, From-only fallback, MIME parse-back, References, control characters, groups, multiple recipients, and zero send invocations on denial. This is syntactic conformance plus offline tests, not whole-program provider proof. No live mailbox, provider message, credential, or send was accessed.
